title: Proper Cleanout Orientation and Access
description: Installing cleanouts in a drainage system is critical for long-term maintenance, but direction matters. A cleanout fitting must always be installed so that the snake or drain cable enters in the direction of the wastewater flow. Installing a cleanout tee backward causes clearing tools to jam or head upstream toward fixtures instead of downstream toward the main sewer. Additionally, maintain adequate clearance around cleanout plugs as required by local plumbing codes to allow technicians to easily remove threaded caps with pipe wrenches without hitting wall studs or adjacent framing.

Proper Cleanout Orientation and Access

Installing cleanouts in a drainage system is critical for long-term maintenance, but direction matters. A cleanout fitting must always be installed so that the snake or drain cable enters in the direction of the wastewater flow. Installing a cleanout tee backward causes clearing tools to jam or head upstream toward fixtures instead of downstream toward the main sewer. Additionally, maintain adequate clearance around cleanout plugs as required by local plumbing codes to allow technicians to easily remove threaded caps with pipe wrenches without hitting wall studs or adjacent framing.
